title: Stale-input signal, tool-path ownership and shadow-output exposure are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 059 Case intake agent in shadow E1b v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 16, 20, 41, 42 and 43; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story reads v_ace_batch_status directly for data_as_of, assembles the five tools through P3 CaseQueryService, P5 DocumentQueryService and P1 CollateralQueryService inside one module, and proves shadow output is hidden by a single GET /admin/agent-runs. In the target P10 rwb-agent owns agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation in rwb_agent and runs AgentRunWorkflow on queue rwb-agent, P3 rwb-case owns case, accounts, contact points, tasks and the timeline, P5 rwb-document owns document and document_field, P1 rwb-source-data is the only reader of the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views and owns the data products and freshness (DP-05), and P4 rwb-access owns masking and permissions. The sources name neither the P1 operation that serves the business-date freshness and the stale-input fact to P10, nor the exact P3, P5 and P1 operations behind each of the five tools, nor which agent-run evidence may be read without exposing the shadow summary or gap flags.
evidence: RWB-E1-059 sections 3, 4 steps 2 to 5, 5 X2 and X5, 7 AC1 and AC5, 11 (DF-CAS-001 to DF-ACE-080, DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-096), 12 (EV-01, EV-28, five tools, intake-summary-v1, POST and GET /admin/agent-evaluations, GET /admin/agent-runs) and 13; Arch v5 slides 15 (P1 GET /freshness and the ACE view contract), 16 (P10 IN/OUT and AgentRunWorkflow 60 s then rule result), 20 (every service), 41 (service catalogue), 42 (EV-01 CaseCreated) and 43 (EV-28 AgentRunCompleted); Ownership Map tables agent_run, agent_sample, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation (P10), recovery_case (P3), document and document_field (P5), data_product and data_product_load (P1), masking_rule (P4), api rows GET /data-products/freshness, GET /data-products/{productCode}/records (P1), GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline, GET /cases/{caseId}/accounts, GET /cases/{caseId}/parties (P3), GET /cases/{caseId}/documents, GET /documents/{documentId} (P5), POST and GET /admin/agent-evaluations, POST /admin/agent-samples, GET /admin/agent-runs, GET /cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs (P10) and GET /me/session (P4).
owner_role: P10 agent owner, P1 source data owner, P3 case owner, P4 access owner and P5 document owner
proposed: Route the stale fact through P1's freshness and data-product contracts, read each tool through its owner's published operation, read shadow-run evidence through the P10 admin and case output reads only, and prove the event and workflow path as set out in ASM-B-ITG-W1-08-E1059-1 to -6.

title: Document-type reference data owner, extraction field reads and the proposal column are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 060 Extraction evaluation E1c v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 16, 20, 41 and 42; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story reads document content and confirmed fields through P5 DocumentQueryService, takes the six document types from LOV-DOC-TYPE through P4, stores the extraction proposal in a new column added to agent_evaluation_run by migration V10_003, and exports the proposal through GET /admin/agent-evaluations. In the target P5 rwb-document owns document and document_field in rwb_document, P10 rwb-agent owns the four evaluation tables in rwb_agent, and reference data is owned by P3 rwb-case under the R-PREC default ruling and DP-07, not by P4. The sources name neither the P3 operation that serves LOV-DOC-TYPE and its version, nor the exact P5 read set for content, fields and confirmed values, nor whether the proposal column remains a P10 migration.
evidence: RWB-E1-060 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 7, 5 X1 to X7, 7 AC1 to AC8, 11 (DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-017, DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-096), 12 (POST /admin/agent-samples, POST and GET /admin/agent-evaluations, DocumentQueryService) and 13 (V10_003__evaluation_proposal.sql, LOV-DOC-TYPE through P4); Arch v5 slides 16 (P5 and P10 IN/OUT), 20 (every service) and 41 (service catalogue); Ownership Map tables document, document_field (P5), agent_sample, agent_run, agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation (P10), lov_value, reference_row, reference_version (P3), api rows GET /documents/{documentId}, GET /documents/{documentId}/content, PATCH /documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}, POST /documents/{documentId}/review (P5), GET /admin/lists/{listCode} (P3), POST /admin/agent-samples, POST and GET /admin/agent-evaluations (P10).
owner_role: P10 agent owner, P5 document owner and P3 case owner
proposed: Read the document types through the P3 reference-data contract, read content and fields through the P5 contract, keep the proposal column in P10's own migration and prove the three approaches on the recorded model stub as set out in ASM-B-ITG-W1-08-E1060-1 to -5.

title: Rule-row owner lookup, interaction ledger read and deviation-absence evidence are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 062 Deviation screening agent in shadow E2b v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 16, 20, 41, 42 and 43; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 11, 12, 14 and 24; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story reads the owner role of each code from rule rows R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06 through a P3 RuleCatalog and calls RuleEvaluator.ownerFor, reads interactions through a P7 InteractionLedgerReader, and proves that shadow raises nothing by asserting no deviation record and deviation_open false. In the target rule rows are owned by P7 rwb-decision under the table ruling and DP-04, the interaction ledger is owned by P1 rwb-source-data under DP-18, deviations are owned by S8 rwb-deviation, and the screening runs inside P10 rwb-agent as AgentRunWorkflow with an embedded Drools kit. The sources name neither the P7 operation that serves the rule rows and their owner roles to P10, nor the P1 ledger read that replaces the P7 reader, nor any S8 read operation with which the suite can prove the absence of a deviation record.
evidence: RWB-E1-062 sections 3, 4 steps 4 and 5, 5 X5, 7 AC1, AC2 and AC4, 11 (DF-REF-002, DF-REF-010, DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-011, DF-CAS-038), 12 (EV-01, EV-16, EV-28, screening-v1, P3 CaseQueryService, P7 InteractionLedgerReader, P3 RuleEvaluator.ownerFor) and 13; Arch v5 slides 15 (S8 IN/OUT), 16 (P10 IN/OUT), 20, 41, 42 (EV-01, EV-16) and 43 (EV-28); Temporal and Drools design slides 11 (embedded Drools and own schema), 12 (L4 activities EvaluateRules and RecordAndApply), 14 (event, signal, EvaluateRules, RecordAndApply) and 24 (S8 source rule set); Ownership Map tables rule_row, rule_package, rule_package_version (P7), interaction (P1), deviation (S8), agent_run, agent_evaluation_run and agent_evaluation (P10), api rows GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions (P1), GET /admin/rule-packages and GET /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions (P7), GET /cases/{caseId}, GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline (P3), POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations and PATCH /deviations/{deviationId} (S8; no S8 read operation is listed).
owner_role: P10 agent owner, P7 decision owner, P1 source data owner, S8 deviation owner and P4 access owner
proposed: Evaluate the code and owner role from the P7 rule package through the embedded Drools kit, read interactions through P1's ledger contract, prove the absence of a deviation through the P3 case read and the absence of rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1, and keep every code and role in data as set out in ASM-B-ITG-W1-08-E1062-1 to -6.

title: Data lake removed: agent daily read model, reporting read and job rerun owner are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 063 Agent monitoring dashboard v1 E2c v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 17, 20, 37, 41, 42, 43 and 44; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story copies daily agent runs to the data lake table agent_run_daily through a P10 step inside JOB-15 at 01:30, matches the row count against the source, sends a cost alert through the P6 notification interface and lets the Power BI report read the lake copy. In the target the data lake and INT-19 and INT-20 are removed (DP-17), reporting is owned by P9 rwb-reporting and fed from events, JOB-15 is an Airflow trigger in rwb-reporting, the admin job view and rerun are owned by P1 rwb-source-data, and the alert still goes through P6 rwb-comms. The sources name neither the P9 read model operation and row shape that replace agent_run_daily, nor how the P10 daily step hands its measures to P9, nor which service owns the JOB-15 record in the target.
evidence: RWB-E1-063 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 5, 5 X1 to X5, 7 AC1 to AC7, 11 (DF-AGT-037 to DF-AGT-111), 12 (JOB-15 at 01:30, agent_run_daily, GET and POST /admin/jobs, AgentRunExtractSource) and 13; Arch v5 slides 15 (P9 measures and extract), 17 (P6 notification path), 20 (JOB-11 outbox relay), 37 (no data lake), 41, 42, 43 and 44 (JOB-15 Airflow trigger, no data lake); Ownership Map tables agent_run, agent_policy, agent_alert (P10), measure_definition, measure_snapshot, measure_publish (P9), notice, template (P6), job_catalog, outbound_item (P2), api rows GET /reports/measures (P9), GET /admin/agent-metrics (P10), GET /admin/jobs and POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun (P1).
owner_role: P10 agent owner, P9 reporting owner, P1 source data owner, P6 comms owner and P2 integration owner
proposed: Replace the lake copy with the P9 reporting read model fed from the agent events and the P10 daily step, read it through GET /reports/measures, keep the count check and the alert rule, and read JOB-15 through P1's admin job operations as set out in ASM-B-ITG-W1-08-E1063-1 to -6.

title: Reference-load operation owner, ACE view value read and contract confirmation form are not named for the target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 064 Data dictionary for the 14 data products v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 12 and 13); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 20, 29 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story loads the governance rows for sys_fields through POST /admin/reference-loads and applies them inside P1, reads the days_past_due value through a P1 view query, and records the ACE team lead's confirmation as a role, a date and a stored document reference. In the target the reference-load operations are owned by P3 rwb-case under the R-PREC default ruling, while sys_objects, sys_fields, sys_field_version, data_product and data_contract stay with P1 rwb-source-data, and only P1 reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views. The sources name neither the P3 operation set through which the load is submitted, approved and verified, nor the P1 data-product read that replaces the suite's own view query, nor the document-reference form of the ACE team confirmation.
evidence: RWB-E1-064 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 10, 5 X1 to X7, 7 AC1 to AC8, 11 (DF-REF-088 to DF-REF-115, DF-OPS-010 to DF-OPS-020), 12 (GET and PATCH /admin/data-dictionary/fields, GET and PATCH /admin/data-contracts, POST /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}/publish, POST /admin/reference-loads, DataDictionaryLoader) and 13; Arch v5 slides 15 (P1 view contract and freshness), 20, 29 (only P1 reads the views) and 41; Ownership Map tables sys_objects, sys_fields, sys_field_version, data_product, data_contract, data_product_access, data_product_load (P1), reference_row, reference_version, parameter_catalog (P3), api rows GET and PATCH /admin/data-dictionary/fields, GET and PATCH /admin/data-contracts, POST /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}/publish, GET /data-products/{productCode}/records, GET /data-products/freshness (P1), POST /admin/reference-loads and its approve, verify and rollback (P3).
owner_role: P1 source data owner, P3 case owner and P4 access owner
proposed: Drive the load through P3's reference-load contract, apply and read it through P1's dictionary contract, read the ACE value through P1's data-product records, and keep the confirmation as role, date and document reference as set out in ASM-B-ITG-W1-08-E1064-1 to -6.
